title: Weighings and the least information needed

sections.skill: Plan weighings or questions and find the least number that always identifies the answer

questions.prompt: A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. There are 9 coins and one is heavier. What is the least number of weighings that always finds the heavy coin?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. There are 9 coins and one is heavier. Which first weighing lets you always finish in the fewest total weighings?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. With 3 weighings you can always find the heavier coin among 27 coins.

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. What is the largest number of coins n for which 2 weighings always find the one heavier coin?
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: n == 9 (example: n = 9)

sections.skill: Strategy: each weighing has three outcomes
sections.relationship: Students weigh half against half. Remembering that a weighing has three outcomes (left down, right down, balance) leads to splitting the suspects into three groups.
sections.author_note: Students weigh half against half. Remembering that a weighing has three outcomes (left down, right down, balance) leads to splitting the suspects into three groups.

lesson.title: Each weighing has three outcomes
text: A weighing can tip left, tip right or balance: three outcomes.
Split the suspects into three groups as equal as possible: two on the scale (same size) and one off it.
After w weighings there are at most 3 x 3 x ... (w times) outcome patterns, so at most that many coins can be told apart.

example.title: Worked example (a different count)
prompt: There are 3 coins and one is heavier. How many weighings?
steps: Weigh coin 1 against coin 2. If one goes down, it is heavy. If they balance, coin 3 is heavy.

questions.prompt: How many different outcomes can one weighing on a balance scale have?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. With 3 coins and one heavier, one weighing always finds the heavy coin.

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. There are 5 coins and one is heavier. You weigh 2 against 2 and they balance. What do you know?

choices.text: The fifth coin is the heavy one.
You must weigh again to know.
One of the four weighed coins is heavy.

questions.correct_answer: The fifth coin is the heavy one.

questions.prompt: How many outcome patterns do 2 weighings have in all?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. With 4 coins and one heavier, one weighing always finds the heavy coin.

questions.prompt: A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. You may use 4 weighings. What is the largest number of coins among which you can always find the one heavier coin?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. There are 6 coins and one is heavier. You weigh 2 against 2 and the left side goes down. Which next weighing is sure to identify the heavy coin?

choices.text: The two coins left off against each other
One left-side coin against the other left-side coin
One right-side coin against one coin that was left off the scale

questions.correct_answer: One left-side coin against the other left-side coin

questions.prompt: You have 3 weights of different sizes and compare them two at a time on a balance. Finding the heaviest always takes at least 2 weighings.
You have 8 weights of different sizes and compare them two at a time on a balance. What is the least number of weighings that always finds the heaviest?

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. Give a number of coins n from 20 to 30 for which 3 weighings always find the one heavier coin.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 20 and n <= 27 (example: n = 27)

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. Why can 2 weighings NOT always find the heavy coin among 10?

choices.text: Two weighings give only 9 outcome patterns, but there are 10 possible heavy coins.
You cannot put 5 coins on each side.
The first weighing must use all 10 coins.

questions.correct_answer: Two weighings give only 9 outcome patterns, but there are 10 possible heavy coins.

questions.prompt: A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. With 4 coins and one heavier, 2 weighings always find the heavy coin.

A balance scale compares two groups of coins: one side goes down, or the two sides balance. All coins look the same. All genuine coins weigh the same; the one odd coin is heavier unless the question says otherwise. Give a number of coins n from 20 to 90 for which 3 weighings are NOT enough but 4 weighings are enough to always find the one heavier coin.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 28 and n <= 81 (example: n = 50)
